owner_decisions: Provider mix and spend ceiling. Options: (a) Haiku 5.5 for every live role, verdict included; (b) Haiku workers with a Sonnet 5.5 verdict; (c) Sonnet-only. Recommend (a), with Sonnet used off-clock only (judge escalations, gold verdicts, Batch at 50%) and a second dark flag for a Sonnet verdict that flips only if the fragrance eval shows a gap. Set a Console workspace spend limit at or below $400 and a monthly cap of about $50. Why: (a) gives 14.5 months of runway at 300/day cached (R1), Sonnet-only gives 0.7, and Sonnet's measured TTFT of about 11 s cannot fit a sub-10 s verdict (R9).

Moderation and the processor list. Options: keep OpenAI omni-moderation, so two named processors; or replace L3/L4 with a Haiku classifier and drop OpenAI. Recommend keeping OpenAI moderation through 1.0.x and naming both processors in the new legal text, then replacing it behind a flag when the legal text next changes. Why: it is free and fail-open today (content_safety_service.py:234-262), and the consent re-ask happens anyway (A1).

Consent re-ask and switch sequencing. Options: (a) switch text roles by OTA after approval, with privacy/terms/landing/processors.json and AI_CONSENT_VERSION 3, keeping camera vision on OpenAI until 1.0.1; (b) wait for 1.0.1 and switch everything at once. Recommend (a), and make the 1.0.1 permission strings provider-neutral ('our AI providers'). Why: app.json:220/:228 and locales/en.json:4-5 say photos are 'sent to OpenAI', and those strings are native, so a camera switch before 1.0.1 makes the permission prompt untrue (A1, verified).

Anthropic server tools and the robots ruling. Options: (a) ban web_search/web_fetch; (b) allow web_search only on a KB miss (max_uses 1-2, blocked_domains fragrantica/parfumo/basenotes), with discovered URLs fetched by our own robots-gated fetcher and never web_fetch; (c) also allow web_fetch on registry hosts. Recommend (b). Why: web_fetch's handling of an unreadable robots.txt is undocumented, so it cannot be shown to meet the fail-closed ruling (R2), while web_search returns only URLs we then fetch under our own rules (A4, R4).

Robots on the live per-request PDP fetch. Options: keep the ruling's current scope (the live user-requested fetch is not a robots surface, per ruling.md:235) and apply robots only to the new KB crawler; or extend fail-closed robots to the live path using registry robots_state. Recommend applying it to the crawler now, and making the live path skip hosts whose kb_merchants robots_state is disallowed or unreadable once the registry carries that state. Why: an owned, auto-growing KB turns repeat per-request fetches into crawling in effect.

'Challenge = stop' versus shipped tools. Options: retire SCRAPEDO_SUPER and the Zyte sephora.me seed, and close #93 as won't-do; or keep them for render-only SPA literals (megamart, alosra, noon) that are not challenge walls. Recommend retiring super mode and the sephora.me seed and keeping the plain render wave only for non-challenged SPA rows. Why: Scrape.do advertises 'anti-bot bypass' and sephora.me is Akamai-walled (A3).

Data sources to license. Options: Wikidata brands (CC0); Open Beauty Facts (ODbL, kept as a separate collective table); Fragella; Fragrances of the World; UPCitemdb free tier. Recommend Wikidata now for the brand registry, OBF later for skincare/makeup in its own table with attribution, no Fragella (its s3.3 forbids the caching an owned KB needs, and its data may derive from Fragrantica), and a written-licence request to FOTW only if KB coverage lags. Why: R4's licence reading.

FragranceX CJ feed. Options: apply to the CJ program and request written permission for storage, GCC display and image use; or drop it. Recommend applying, with no engineering until written terms arrive, and keeping the crawl rejected. Why: robots/sitemap/PDP all returned 403 cf-mitigated (PLAN_S80.md:32, :71), and directories conflict on whether a feed exists (R4).

Quota rule: 3 per day per device. Options for multiple accounts on one device: the device cap binds across accounts, or per-account only. For the monthly cap: keep 10/month or drop it. For premium: exempt from the device key or not (it has no purchase path, ToS:25). For reset time: UTC (03:00 Bahrain, consistent with PLAN B9) or Riyadh midnight. Recommend: free use allowed only while both the account and the device are under 3/day; keep 10/month until the KB lowers cost; exempt premium/admin; keep the UTC keys but show resets_at to the user. For build 3, which sends no header, fall back to account-only plus a metric. Why: A7/R5. Changing the day boundary mid-flight double-grants or under-grants for one day, and B9 has already ruled 'no key timezone change'. The ToS 'each account' wording changes through U8.

Supabase auth path. Options: move the backend's GoTrue calls to a secret API key with Sb-Forwarded-For enabled, or raise the dashboard per-IP limits. Recommend doing both, plus custom SMTP, before any marketing push. Why: every user shares the Railway egress IP's 30 sign-ups and 150 /token per 5 min buckets (R5; auth_service.py:181 builds the anon-key client).

Share channels to support first. Options: a link-first OTA set (WhatsApp via wa.me, Copy, X, Telegram, SMS/Email, More) now, and native Instagram Stories/Snapchat Creative Kit in 1.0.1 with an image card; or wait and do everything in 1.0.1. Recommend the link-first OTA set after approval, plus landing OG tags now. Decide separately whether to build an image share card and register Meta and Snap Kit apps for 1.0.1. Skip TikTok. Why: R6. The text-only path has no link today, and open.html has 0 og: tags and an empty APP_STORE_URL (verified).

B4 URL-MODE-V2 (fix round 2 NOT_READY on 83daa8cb: MAJOR-R1 same_url drops the query). Options: finish round 3 with both adversaries and merge dark; park it; or fold it into the KB work. Recommend finishing round 3 and merging dark. Why: it removes the 'Unknown Product' success, and its JSON-LD image normaliser (_jsonld_image_urls) is exactly what KB ingest reuses (A4 loss path 7). The work is one fix round from done (NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT_S81).

B2 RESULT-GATE (spec APPROVE_WITH_CHANGES, BL1/BL2). Options: build it now and merge dark, or defer. Recommend writing RULINGS_B2, building it and merging dark, with the flip sized by B1 counts, and adding a category_unsupported reason so the fragrance-only gate shares the same refund envelope. Why: KB writes must reuse the same assess_result identity rules to avoid KB poisoning (A2, R9).

Hidden categories. Options: client-only chip hiding, or adding a backend allowlist gate (ENABLE_CATEGORY_ALLOWLIST) that refuses with a refund. Also decide whether skincare/makeup 'coming soon' chips are tappable and record the tap only. Recommend both the client and backend changes, with tap-only chips shipped after approval. Why: the chip is only a hint and name detection runs every category (scs:483-492, A5). Check Apple Guideline 2.1/2.3 on placeholder features first.

Cohort and survey copy. Options: remove CohortBadge entirely, or reword it as 'Based on a survey of N people like you'; keep or remove the true onboarding survey lines. Recommend removing the badge and keeping the survey lines, which carry no digits. Why: the count is the survey cell size, not the number of shoppers who picked this winner (A5).

Price staleness shown to users. Options: 24 h, 7 days or up to 30 days with an 'as of' date. Recommend fresh at 24 h converted / 7 days genuine, stale up to 30 days shown with its date and refreshed in the background, and no price after that. Why: R9's stale-while-revalidate mirrors price_service.py:134-149.
plan_decisions: Adapter shape. Use app/services/llm_adapter.py (the PLAN R-A12 Protocol), routed per ROLE (parse, classify, extract, vision, verdict, critic) so text and camera can sit on different providers. Cost ledger. A provider-neutral llm_pricing with claude-* rows (input, cache write 5m/1h, cache read, output, the Haiku over-100K tier), plus $0.01 per web_search request. Normalise prompt = input + cache_creation + cache_read. metadata.openai stays byte-identical with the flag OFF; metadata.llm appears only with the flag ON. Fix the hardcoded mini rates (openai_service.py:569-574, 676-684; scs:9606-9610) and make DAILY_4O_CAP provider-aware. Reason: A1, R1.

Pins move in the same PR as the adapter: widen the claude-* model-literal regex (test_model_config.py:135), add messages.create to the U3c AST rule (:99) and AsyncAnthropic to T7b (test_legal_docs_u8.py:763), and set AnthropicIntegration(include_prompts=False) with an updated BASE_INTEGRATIONS. Choose the anthropic SDK pin with the 14-day rule (1.12.x now qualifies). Reason: A1, R2.

Caching layout. Order: tools sorted, then a frozen global system block, then a per-category static block with cache_control at 1 h TTL, then messages with date, lang, cohort, quality flags, the KB card bundle and the query. Split build_verdict_prompt (extraction_service.py:2124-2198) so cohort text sits after the breakpoint. Pre-warm each category at boot. Assert cache_read_input_tokens > 0 in a probe. The critic prompt (about 300 tokens) will not cache. Reason: R1, R2.

KB schema: migration 045, one dark file, RLS service-role only with the 044 REVOKE pattern. Tables: kb_products (canonical id = hash of category + dedup_brand_name + _strip_identity_axes), kb_variants (_identity_cache_token), kb_offers (merchant, amount, currency, source_method, url, title, in_stock, captured_at, plus a latest-per-merchant view and a prune cron), kb_images (URL + source page + verified_at only, never the file), kb_specs (field, value, source_url, extractor, model), kb_reviews (source, rating, count, provenance), kb_merchants, kb_feedback. Harden the 012 policies after the live read. Provenance is honest, with no 'gpt' default, and tier-3 model knowledge is excluded. Reason: A2, A4, R4.

KB write points. One fire_and_forget kb_ingest right after build_comparison_response on REST, stream and camera, behind ENABLE_KB_INGEST (read per call, a no-op when OFF). Write only when B1 assess_result is supported and identity confidence passes, and never write placeholder identities. Also persist the JSON-LD cand['image'] (price_service.py:10962-10964), the resolved PDP URL per host, and host health from _record_provider_attempt (scs:141-169). Reason: A2, A3, A4, R9.

KB read points. ENABLE_KB_FIRST_SERVE reads both products' cards in one round trip before _fetch_product_data and returns early on a full hit. The unified-search gate also consults KB/L2, not only L1 (scs:5858-5860). Offers are served stale-while-revalidate with an as-of date. A pair verdict cache keyed on (card versions, price band, lang, persona bucket, model, prompt sha) is wired through the unused set_comparison_cache (cache_service.py:770-778). The crown is frozen per response. Reason: A2, A9, R9.

Registry growth loop. kb_merchants is seeded from bh_gcc_sources.json (including the country/genuine_method the loader drops, and the 400 candidate rows), read per call so admitting a host needs no restart. Fields: platform plus confidence, adapter, search_template, robots {state, status, fetched_at, body_sha, crawl_delay, next_reread}, health, challenge {vendor, parked_until}, deny, tos_reviewed_at. It runs off-clock only. Discovery inputs: search results already paid for, robots-declared sitemaps, Common Crawl CDX, brand where-to-buy pages. A candidate becomes live only after a robots read, a platform probe and one validated sample PDP. Reason: A2, A3, R3.

Crawler politeness and legal guards. Fetch as QarenBot with a contact URL, never impersonating Chrome. Robots fail-closed (404/410 allow-all, any other non-2xx or timeout skip). Per-host concurrency 1, delay = max(Crawl-delay, 2 s), backoff honouring Retry-After. Any challenge parks the host and stops; never rotate UA, IP or proxy. One shared DENY_HOSTS module (fragrantica, parfumo, basenotes) used by source_router (drop the literal at source_router.py:347), URL mode, KB ingest and web_search blocked_domains. Protego serves as test oracle and Crawl-delay parser; Scrapy, Crawlee and Firecrawl are not used. Classify the 199 blank-mechanism live rows with detect_platform first. Reason: A3, R3.

Latency budget, validated with stage_timings_ms. KB hit: cards under 2 s, verdict under 3 s cached or under 7 s streamed on Haiku. Cold: names under 2 s, per-product partial cards under 12 s, verdict under 20 s, cap 25 s inside the 30 s hard cap (do not raise it). First fix the /health stalls (p95 8.4 s). Move smart fallback and Tier 2/3 to background enrichment, start the image race before the unified search with an early stash, and emit per-product SSE events. Reason: A9, R9.

Client speed (OTA after approval unless noted). Skip the 1.2 s floor on a fast hit and shorten the 800 ms reveal. Use getSentryExpoConfig with replay and feedback off (-198,567 B). Drop the runtime Geist load after the device check. Lazy-load Legal, Paywall, onboarding and ScanCamera. Set freezeOnBlur on the Main tabs and stale-while-revalidate on History. Flip SSE only after the #118 pinning check. expo-image and embedded Cairo wait for 1.0.1. Reason: A6, R8.

Rate limits and device quota. Add ENABLE_DEVICE_DAILY_QUOTA: consume usage:daily:dev:{HMAC(pepper, fp)} in the same atomic consume as the account key and refund both on the existing paths. Fingerprint source order: header, then users.device_fingerprint_hash, then account-only with a metric. The client sends X-Device-Fingerprint on every metered request; 1.0.1 swaps osBuildId for an app UUID/IDFV. Report resets_at through B9 USAGE-STATUS-V2 rather than a new field. Reason: A7, R5, PLAN_S80.md:65.

Auth throttling. Add ENABLE_AUTH_THROTTLE_V2 with Upstash counters, so they survive deploys. Add per-email limits on register, reset and resend, and switch the lockout to backoff so a locked user can still reset. Fix the proxy anchor to the rightmost trusted hop before any IP-keyed flag; the leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry at rate_limiter.py:33-49 is forgeable. Replace the string-presence tests with per-route AST decorator pins. Reason: A7, R5.

Share implementation. A per-channel message builder from the unused referrals.share.message template and the privacy toggles: wa.me, x.com/intent/tweet with separate url and hashtags, t.me/share/url, sms/mailto, a real expo-clipboard Copy, and Linking.openURL in try/catch instead of canOpenURL. The link is always present and '30 seconds' is removed. Static OG first, then ENABLE_SHARE_PREVIEW_HTML for per-token OG built from resolve_invite's sanitized data. Track share_target_opened, not share_completed. Reason: R6, A5.

Critique loop. No inline regeneration (ENABLE_SELF_CRITIQUE stays OFF; only the B1/B2 deterministic gate runs inline). A client-generated compare_request_id travels on the compare, /feedback and /events. A compare_judgements row is written after delivery: B1 programmatic tags, a Haiku Batch judge that sees the evidence, Sonnet escalation on a 'No', a flag or a 5% sample, and a grounded check on disputes with allowed_domains = registry. The judge never grades its own output. Reason: R7, A8.

Feedback and learning output. A two-question card (identity first, then one rotating price/specs/choice question mapped to the existing winner_correct/price_correct/specs_correct and C6 chips). ContactUs moves out of comparison_feedback. A nightly cluster job proposes KB corrections (grounded evidence plus at least 2 devices) and owner-reviewed exemplar sets stored in the DB, not the container JSON. Fix the behaviour-profile select. Add a Claude arm to shadow_experiments and a 60+ case fragrance gold set. Reason: R7, A8, A5.

Assumptions:
1. Prices are from platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing (R1, read 2026-10-22). Haiku 5.5: $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok for prompts up to 100K tokens; cache write $0.125 (5 min) or $0.20 (1 h); cache read $0.01. Sonnet 5.5: $2 in / $10 out; cache writes $2.50 / $4; cache read $0.10. The bundled skill's $0.20 for a Sonnet cache read is wrong. web_search costs $10 per 1,000 searches; a failed search is not billed. Batch is 50% off and stacks with caching.
2. The token model is R1's and is inferred, not measured. Workers (parse, 2x specs, 2x price, 2x reviews, critic) use about 15,000 input and 2,400 output tokens. The verdict uses about 5,900 input and 900 output. Cacheable prefixes are about 6,100 worker tokens and 2,900 verdict tokens. All counts are code prompt lengths times 1.3 for the Claude tokenizer. Three searches add about 25,000 input tokens, extrapolated from the docs' one-search example of 6,039.
3. 'Cached' means 1-hour TTL prefix writes, amortised at 24 writes per day per prefix. A month is 30.4 days. Runway is $400 divided by the monthly cost. Rows marked 'derived' are my arithmetic on R1's per-compare figures.
4. Thinking is disabled or set to effort low. Leaving it on adds about $0.0008 per compare on Haiku workers and about $0.01 on a Sonnet verdict (R1).
5. The table excludes Serper (about $0.003 per compare at $0.001 a call, until the KB cuts it), OpenAI moderation (free), retries and refusals.
6. Sensitivity: R2's larger token model (25K in / 4K out, about $0.005 for Haiku workers) would add about 55% to the Haiku rows. R2 derived it from a mis-sized parser prompt (contradiction 1), so R1 is preferred.
7. Any Haiku request above 100K prompt tokens, cached tokens included, costs 5x. Search results must be capped with max_uses.
8. The Start tier has a $500 monthly spend cap. Sonnet-only with search reaches it at about 100 compares a day.
9. Switching provider ends OpenAI's free daily allowance from data sharing (CLAUDE.md:556), so the cash bill can rise even where the list price falls.
10. The real per-compare cost is a blend of the cold and KB-warm rows, weighted by the unmeasured KB hit rate (unverified item 7). R2 and R9 give a cold Sonnet-verdict compare with 3-4 searches at $0.03-0.06, consistent with the Haiku + Sonnet + search row.
merged_architecture:
1 PROVIDER ADAPTER (A1, R2, PLAN R-A12). llm_adapter.py routes per role (parse, classify, extract, vision, verdict, critic) to OpenAIAdapter (byte-identical guarded_llm_create) or a real AnthropicAdapter. The Anthropic side runs through guarded_anthropic_create: its own breaker, typed-exception classification, no store kwarg. It returns an OpenAI-shaped object, so call sites stay. Claude calls send no temperature; Haiku runs with thinking disabled at effort low; small token caps are raised; output_config.format is used at every JSON site (B3 V2 schema reused); a refusal maps to LLMUnavailableError. Default is Haiku 5.5 for every live role; Sonnet 5.5 runs off-clock only (R1, R9). Moderation stays on OpenAI for now. Camera vision stays on OpenAI until 1.0.1 ships new permission strings (app.json:220/228). Ledger: llm_pricing with claude rows plus web_search; metadata.openai stays byte-identical with the flag OFF.

2 KNOWLEDGE BASE (A2, A4, R4, R9). Migration 045, RLS service-role only. Tables: kb_products (canonical id), kb_variants, kb_offers (captured_at), kb_images (URL and provenance only), kb_specs (source_url), kb_reviews, kb_feedback. The 012 tables are hardened after a live policy read.
- Write: kb_ingest after build_comparison_response (ENABLE_KB_INGEST), only when B1 rates the result supported and identity confidence passes (the B2 rules), which guards against poisoning. Also stores the JSON-LD image and the PDP URL per host.
- Read: ENABLE_KB_FIRST_SERVE runs before _fetch_product_data. Offers are served stale-while-revalidate with an as-of date. The search gate reads the KB, not just L1.

3 MERCHANT REGISTRY LOOP (A3, R3). kb_merchants is seeded from bh_gcc_sources (275 live rows plus candidates) and read per call. Fields: platform, adapter, robots state, health, challenge parked_until, deny.
- An off-clock worker discovers hosts from search results already paid for, robots-declared sitemaps, Common Crawl CDX and brand where-to-buy pages.
- A host goes live only after a QarenBot robots read (fail-closed), a platform probe and one validated sample PDP.
- Politeness: one request at a time per host, delay = max(Crawl-delay, 2 s), backoff on 429/503. Any challenge parks the host and stops. Never rotate UA, IP or proxy; the crawler uses a named UA.
- One DENY_HOSTS list is shared by the router, URL mode, ingest and web_search blocked_domains.
- web_search runs only on a KB miss (max_uses 1-2), and its URLs go to our own fetcher. Never web_fetch.

4 CACHING (R1, R2, A9). Order: sorted tools, then the frozen system block, then a per-category block with cache_control (1 h), then messages carrying lang, cohort, KB cards and the query. Pre-warm at boot and assert cache reads. A pair verdict cache keyed on card versions, price band, lang, persona, model and prompt sha uses the unused set_comparison_cache. The crown is frozen per response.

5 LATENCY BUDGET (A9, R9, A6, R8). Fix the /health stalls first.
- KB hit: cards under 2 s; verdict under 3 s cached, under 7 s streamed.
- Cold: names under 2 s, partial cards under 12 s, verdict under 20 s, cap 25 s.
- Phase-2 and Tier 2/3 move to background enrichment. The image race starts early, with an early stash. SSE events go out per product.
- Client: a fast-hit floor skip, and the SSE flip after the pinning device check.

6 RATE LIMITS (A7, R5). Auth throttles in Upstash, per-email limits on sign-up and reset, a trusted proxy hop, and Supabase Sb-Forwarded-For. The device daily key is consumed in the same atomic call as the account key, with refunds to both and an account-only fallback for build 3. resets_at comes through B9.

7 SHARE (R6, A5). A per-channel builder (wa.me, X intent, Telegram, SMS/email, real Copy, OS sheet). A link in every message, no '30 seconds'. Static OG tags, then a per-token preview page; native kits in 1.0.1.

8 CRITIQUE LOOP (R7, A8). No inline regeneration. A client compare_request_id ties feedback to the compare. A judgement row per compare: B1 tags, a Haiku Batch judge that sees the evidence, Sonnet escalation, a grounded check on disputes. A nightly job turns failure clusters into KB correction proposals, owner-reviewed exemplars and eval cases, fed by a two-question feedback card.
